newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds match gains in Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds match gains in Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose along with Treasuries Thursday afternoon, possibly on the strength of agency buying, traders and analysts said.
"Obviously, the conventionals have an agency bid behind them, and I heard they were active this morning," said one Midwest-based portfolio manager.
Retail activity was less pronounced. "Its been fairly quiet," an East Coast trader said.
Thirty-year pass-throughs were up about 10/32 to 12/32 in current and discount coupons late on Thursday.
Ginnie Mae discounts briefly surged ahead early in the afternoon, but moved back in line with Freddies and Fannies later. One trader said agency buying probably accounted for the spurt.

In late-afternoon trading, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.0-percent coupons were up 8/32 at 99-01/32. Current-coupon Fannie Maes were up 7/32 at 100-25/32, and comparable Freddie Macs had climbed 7/32 to 99-02/32.
Treasuries and mortgage-backeds started off slightly negative, despite benign reports on consumer prices and retail sales.
The early losses reversed in part because of short covering and swap buying, Treasuries traders said.

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent in October, matching its September performance. Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.2 percent, compared with a 0.3 percent increase the month before.
Retail sales rose a slight 0.2 percent last month, down from a 0.8 percent rise in September. Excluding automobiles, sales rose 0.4 percent, slightly below their 0.5 percent September increase.
